The text explicitly lists both options, allowing the creature to choose either ability. Therefore, using Acrobatics is permitted.

The rule 'making-an-attack > melee-attacks > grappling' states that to make a grapple, you must use 'at least one free hand'. The question asks if you can hold a grapple with one hand (implying the other hand is occupied holding the weapon) and still attack. Since the grapple rule explicitly requires at least one free hand to seize the target, holding a two-handed weapon in both hands would leave no free hand to make the grapple check. Therefore, you cannot hold a grapple with one hand (while wielding a two-handed weapon) because the act of grappling itself demands a free hand.

The rule for shoving states that if you win the contest, you can 'push it 5 feet away from you'. The rule for being prone states that to stand up, a creature must spend movement equal to half its speed. The rule for grappled creatures states their speed becomes 0. Therefore, a creature that is both grappled and shoved away has its speed reduced to 0 (due to the grapple) and is pushed away. Since standing up requires spending movement, and a creature with speed 0 cannot spend movement to stand up (the rule explicitly says 'You can't stand up if you don't have enough movement left or if your speed is 0'), the creature cannot stand up immediately after being shoved while grappled. The conclusion turns on the phrase 'speed becomes 0' in the grappled condition and 'if your speed is 0' in the standing up rule. The text does not allow another reading where a creature with speed 0 could somehow generate movement to stand.

The question asks what is rolled when an invisible attacker hits an invisible target. The rule 'damage-and-healing > damage-rolls' states that you roll the damage die or dice and apply the damage to your target. The rules on attack rolls ('making-an-attack > attack-rolls') and modifiers ('making-an-attack > attack-rolls > rolling-1-or-20', 'conditions > invisible') determine whether the attack hits or misses, but do not specify what is rolled if the attack hits.
